title: Egg Drop With 2 Eggs and N Floors
summary: Given two identical eggs and a building with n floors, find the minimum number of moves to determine the critical floor f where an egg breaks above f but not at or below f.
statement: Given two identical eggs and a building with n floors, find the minimum number of moves to determine the critical floor f where an egg breaks above f but not at or below f. In each move, an unbroken egg can be dropped from any floor, and if it breaks, it cannot be used again.
constraints: There are exactly two identical eggs.
Determine the threshold in the worst case using the fewest drops.
reference_solution:
def minimum_two_egg_drop_moves(n):
    moves = 0
    covered = 0
    while covered < n:
        moves += 1
        covered += moves
    return moves
hints: If the first drop is x floors above the last safe floor, a break leaves x-1 floors for the final egg.
Choose successive gaps m, m-1, ..., 1 so both break and survival leave at most one fewer move.
The smallest m whose triangular number m(m+1)/2 reaches n is sufficient.
No m moves can cover more than the same triangular total with two eggs, while the decreasing-gap strategy attains it, proving minimality.
editorial: No m moves can cover more than the same triangular total with two eggs, while the decreasing-gap strategy attains it, proving minimality.

tests.explanation: Dropping from either floor first may require a second drop, so the answer is two.
Fourteen moves cover only 105 floors cumulatively, while thirteen cover 91; therefore fourteen is minimal.
